I’ve been off for a few months—not like I’m failing at life, but nothing feels like it matters. I’ve cried over small things, even grading papers. My wife says she’s worried because I haven’t touched the garden, and usually I’m out there every weekend. I keep thinking... what if something bad happens to my students because I missed something? Not that I’ve done anything wrong—but I feel responsible, like I should’ve prevented things I can’t even control. Once I found myself standing in the garage with a bottle of pills, not sure how I got there. I didn’t do it—but I had them.

Before that, about three weeks in the spring, I was the opposite—up late planning new lessons, redoing the whole curriculum, starting DIY projects at home, calling parents at odd hours. I’d feel great one minute and snap at my wife the next for no reason. I couldn’t stick to one thing—started rewriting a novel, then painting the basement, then organizing every filing cabinet. But I didn’t miss work, and I kept things together—just felt like I was running on a different setting.

It’s just... I don’t know which version is me. And I’m scared the low phase will come back.

D009-D003_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now. There are days when everything feels heavy—I don’t want to get out of bed, talking takes effort, and even tattooing, which I love, feels like work. I don’t feel joy in much anymore. My clients notice I’m quieter than usual, slower to respond. That low mood stuck around so long I started wondering if this was just who I am now.

But then, about three months ago, something shifted. I didn’t plan it, but I suddenly had this burst of energy. I was taking on extra clients, working late, even planning to open my own shop. I felt great—really alive, like I could go all night. And I *did*—I’d sleep two, maybe three hours and wake up ready. I wasn’t jittery or talking over people, just… motivated. Not anxious, just *up*. It didn’t mess with my work—in fact, it helped at first.

Problem is, now it’s fading, and that dullness is creeping back. I can’t tell if what I had was a break from depression or something else. I’ve always been restless, sure—but I don’t remember it being like this as a kid. It’s confusing, because part of me misses that energy, but I don’t want to crash again.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D009-D003_h022.question:
I’ve been feeling all over the place for over a year now—like I’m stuck in this cycle I can’t control. For the past few months, I’ve been super restless, like I can’t sit still even when I try. I’ll pace around my apartment, fidget with wires and gear, pick at my skin—anything to keep moving. I get bursts where I feel electric, almost high, like I can edit videos for hours without breaking a sweat. My sleep drops to four hours and I don’t feel tired—actually feel kind of sharp, in a way. But then out of nowhere, I’ll snap into irritation over tiny things, like a client’s email or background noise.  

But most of the time, it’s this heavy numbness. For like a year, I haven’t really felt joy—from my work, music, nothing. I drag myself through projects, but it takes forever because I’m so drained. Some days I cry for no reason, just break down mid-edit. I want to stop, but I can’t. I’m either moving too fast or too slow, and I don’t know which version of me is real. I’ve always been kind of wound-up, but I can’t say if it started in childhood or just… showed up.

D009-D003_h023.question:
I’ve been feeling really up and down for a while now—like, the past year or so has mostly been a slog. I wake up already exhausted, even if I slept okay. Getting started on tasks feels impossible, and when I do, my body feels heavy, like I’m moving through mud. Some days I just sit at my desk, staring at code that used to flow so easily. It’s been bad enough that I’ve missed deadlines—something that never used to happen.

But then, for about the last three months, things shifted. I don’t know how to explain it—I’m not sad, exactly, but I’m also not quite myself. I’ve been taking on five projects at once, rewriting entire cloud infrastructures overnight, not because they need it, but because I *can*. I sleep maybe four hours and feel fine, like I’ve recharged. One minute I’m excited, full of ideas, and the next, someone says something minor and I want to snap. I don’t feel out of control, but I’m definitely doing too much, too fast.  

I don’t know how long this has all been going on, or if it’s always been this way—I’ve never paid much attention as a kid. It’s just… life feels uneven.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D003_h024.question:

My husband says I’ve been distant, not answering when he talks, not initiating plans with friends like I used to. Emotionally, it’s like I’m numb—nothing touches me, not even things that used to make me cry or laugh.

D009-D003_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for over a year now. Some days, I’m restless—can’t sit still, even at work. I’ll rearrange shelves for no reason, pace during quiet hours at the library, just feel like I *have* to be doing *something*. My mood swings too—suddenly elated, then snapping at a patron over a late book. But it never lasts. No real highs, nothing I’d call mania. I just don’t feel like sleeping much—some nights I’m up until 3 a.m. reading or cleaning, not tired at all. That’s been going on for about three months now, but it’s not like I’m productive. Just… wound up.

But most of the time, it’s the heaviness. For over a year, really. I don’t enjoy knitting anymore. I don’t want to go out. Even walking to the front desk feels slow, like my body’s dragging. I cry in the break room sometimes—don’t know why, just overwhelmed. I’m exhausted no matter how much I rest. 

I’ve always been a little restless, I guess, but I can’t say if it was like this as a kid. And the fast thoughts? Sometimes my mind races, but not enough to finish anything. It’s messy—but not disruptive enough to call it what others describe.
